newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices steady to lower.

text.p: Millfeed prices remained mostly steady to lower on Monday weighed down by lackluster demand and an adequate nearby supply, several dealers said.

"We are heading lower but it is Monday and people seldom do much business on a Monday," a Buffalo dealer said. "We should see five-day flour mill times at least this week, and maybe a little more now that we have the holidays behind us."

Another dealer said Midds were too high-priced forcing the mills to turn to substitutes. "The combination of the two (a pickup in run times and more use of substitutes) was a devastating blow to the (midds) market," he said.
Another dealer agreed, saying feed mills were using more substitutes like corn and soy hulls, which are cheaper.
"Mills are using that for fiber," he said.
Recent warm temperatures in the U.S. Midwest were also a negative factor, dealers said.
"Nationwide, it was pretty warm over the holiday, and my guess is that made the feed business back off a little bit," a Missouri dealer said.
"I think there is a possibility for some substitution in the north but as far as increased run time, that has not had a chance to be a factor yet," he said.
